yolo11n_scratch_control.verdict: this is the fair opponent for Mamba-YOLO-T. At equal (random) initialisation Mamba-YOLO-T 0.8266 BEATS YOLO11n 0.8041 by +0.0225 — the opposite of the naive pretrained-vs-scratch reading. Pretraining alone is worth +0.0714 to YOLO11n (0.8755 pretrained vs 0.8041 scratch), i.e. ~3x the architecture gap.

s3_fair_comparison.protocol: cwd12_sealed.yaml, 100 ep, seeds 101/102/103, V100, sealed 1,977-image holdout
s3_fair_comparison.reading: On 3,671 in-domain images the initialisation choice (+0.071) outweighs the architecture choice (+0.022). Both are real; only the second is an architecture claim.

merge_funnel_2026_08_23.reading: The harvested pool is heavily redundant: dHash dedup removes 44,750 cross-dataset duplicates — the same weed photos re-exported across many Roboflow projects. 'More images' from the web is not the same as more information, and this funnel is why the trainer sees ~59k, not 156k.

tier_ladder_v1_RETRACTED_2026_08_25.why_retracted: the core was taken from the merged corpus's own cottonweed_* files, which the merge's dedup and holdout-stem filter had already stripped by 32% of instances, hitting the rare classes hardest. It scored 0.5601 with ZERO harvested images added, so the gap it was meant to explain existed before any harvested image was involved.
tier_ladder_v1_RETRACTED_2026_08_25.what_it_does_show: within this pipeline the ladder is FLAT — adding 5k/15k/40k harvested images moves the metric by <0.015. Harvested data is close to neutral here, not harmful.
tier_ladder_v1_RETRACTED_2026_08_25.replacement: jobs 44397807 — same ladder with the real cwd12 train split (3,671 imgs, remapped to canonical ids) as the core

tier_ladder_v2_2026_08_25.core: real cwd12 train split (3,671 imgs, 6,131 instances), remapped orig->canonical ids
tier_ladder_v2_2026_08_25.protocol: YOLO11n COCO-pretrained, 100 ep cap, seed 101, nc=100, sealed 1,977-image holdout
tier_ladder_v2_2026_08_25.reading: Adding web-harvested data to a clean in-domain core is essentially FREE and essentially USELESS: +5,000 costs 0.004, +15,000 costs 0.002, and only at +40,000 does a ~0.02 decline appear (still training). The honest cost of scale here is 0.00-0.02, not the 0.27 previously claimed - that figure came from a crippled core (0.5601 with zero harvested images) and was retracted 2026-08-25.
tier_ladder_v2_2026_08_25.residual_note: core+0 reads 0.8636 here vs 0.8755 in the nc=12 sealed run; the ~0.012 difference is the 100-class head carrying 88 unused classes, quantified rather than assumed.
